answers.explanation: Fractional distillation separates miscible liquids with close boiling points, such as liquid air components.
Petroleum, rubber latex, and vulcanizer's solution are mixtures, whereas carbon disulphide is a pure compound.
80 kg of ore with 70% Fe2O3 gives 56 kg Fe2O3 (molar mass 160), yielding (112/160) * 56 = 39.2 kg of iron.
Fixed mass of metal X (0.20 g and 0.40 g) combines with chlorine in a simple ratio (0.36:0.355), illustrating multiple proportions.
Using P1V1 = P2V2 at constant T, (10 * 0.030 dm^3) / 20 dm^3 = 0.015 atm (note: given options A=6.7 atm, B=15.0 atm, C=6.0 atm, D=66.0 atm).
At constant temperature, P1V1 = P2V2 gives V2 = 228 * (750 / 760) = 225 cm^3.
2KHCO3 -> K2CO3 + H2O + CO2; 1000 g KHCO3 (100 g/mol) is 10 mol, giving 5 mol CO2 or 5 * 22.4 = 112 dm^3 at STP.
X (group 2) forms X^2+ and Y (group 7) forms Y^-, giving an ionic compound of formula XY2, not XY.
X^- with 10 electrons has 9 protons (fluorine), and Y^+ with 10 electrons has 11 protons (sodium).
The 3p^3 subshell has three half-filled orbitals, so there are 3 unpaired electrons.
Ammonium chloride (NH4Cl) contains ionic bonding between NH4+ and Cl-, plus a dative covalent bond in NH4+.
Electronegativity increases across a period from left to right: Na < Mg < Al < P < Cl.
Alkaline pyrogallol absorbs oxygen gas, increasing its mass.
Mercury(II) ions (Hg^2+) are toxic heavy metal pollutants even in trace amounts in drinking water.
50 g saturated solution at 100 C (75 g solute per 175 g solution) has 21.43 g salt and 28.57 g water; at 30 C only 7.14 g dissolves, leaving 14.3 g.
Passing excess carbon(IV) oxide into lime water forms soluble calcium hydrogentrioxocarbonate(IV), causing temporary hardness.
Colloidal dispersions scatter light (the Tyndall effect), whereas true solutions do not.
Ammonia and hydrogen chloride are extremely soluble in water, making them ideal for the fountain experiment.
10 cm^3 of 0.1 M Na2CO3 is 0.001 mol, which reacts with excess acid to give 0.001 mol CO2 = 22.4 cm^3 at STP (text shows 224.0 cm^3 due to print typo).
Charge Q = 1.5 * 14400 = 21600 C (0.2238 F); 13.3/118.7 = 0.112 mol Sn, so n = 0.2238 / 0.112 = 2 or 4 depending on printed value.
Na2CO3 and CH3COONa hydrolyze in water to give alkaline solutions with pH greater than 7.
Mn in MnO4^- (+7) is reduced to Mn^2+ (+2), requiring n = 5 electrons.
Sulphur in SO2 (+4) is reduced to S (0) while S in H2S (-2) is oxidized to S (0), so SO2 is the oxidant and H2S is the reductant.
Manganese(IV) oxide acts as a catalyst, lowering the activation energy for hydrogen peroxide decomposition.
1.1 g CaCl2 (111 g/mol) is 0.01 mol; heat released is 50 * 4.18 * 34 = 7106 J (7.11 kJ), or -711 kJ/mol (option A prints -71.1).
The reaction is exothermic (delta H = -89.3 kJ) and decreases gas moles (2 to 1.5), so low temperature and high pressure favour products.
H2(g) + I2(g) <-> 2HI(g) has equal moles of gas on both sides (2 mol), so pressure change has no net effect.
Doubling [NO] from 0.001 to 0.002 increases the rate from 3.0e-5 to 1.2e-4, which is a factor of four.
Dinitrogen oxide (N2O) decomposes on heating to give oxygen-rich gas that rekindles a glowing splint.
Sodium trioxocarbonate(IV) (Na2CO3) is thermally stable and melts without decomposing.
Heating potassium trioxonitrate(V) (KNO3) decomposes it to potassium dioxonitrate(III) and oxygen gas.
Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) turns moist lead(II) trioxonitrate(V) paper black due to lead(II) sulphide formation.
Zn^2+ forms white Zn(OH)2 with aqueous ammonia that dissolves in excess ammonia to form [Zn(NH3)4]^2+.
Bubbling CO2 briefly into clear lime water, Ca(OH)2, forms a white precipitate of insoluble CaCO3.
Copper(II) tetraoxosulphate(VI) is widely used as a fungicide and in agriculture.
Nitrates of mercury and silver decompose on heating to yield the free metal, nitrogen(IV) oxide, and oxygen.
But-2-ene has a symmetrical internal double bond (CH3CH=CHCH3) and exhibits cis-trans geometric isomerism.
Butyl bromide (C4H9Br) has four structural isomers: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, 1-bromo-2-methylpropane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
In the presence of ultraviolet light, alkanes undergo free-radical substitution with chlorine up to tetrachloromethane (CCl4).
10 g propyne (C3H4, 40 g/mol) is 0.25 mol and adds 2 mol Br2 per mole (0.5 mol Br2 = 80 g).
Ethene is absorbed in concentrated H2SO4 to form ethyl hydrogensulphate, which on dilution and warming yields ethanol.
Detergents form soluble calcium and magnesium salts and do not form scum in hard water.
Alcoholic KOH removes H and Br from 2-bromobutane (dehydrohalogenation/elimination) to form but-2-ene.
Propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol) is a viscous, sweet, non-toxic, hygroscopic liquid miscible with water.
The compound is 1-chloro-2-methylpropane, containing a three-carbon main chain with a methyl at C-2 and chloro at C-1.
Complete alkaline hydrolysis of one mole of a triacylglycerol (glyceride) requires 3 moles of NaOH.
Chlorination of ethanoic acid in sunlight substitutes an alpha-hydrogen to yield chloroethanoic acid (ClCH2COOH) and HCl.
